blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (Payment call has no timeout) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Pass an explicit timeout to requests.post (e.g. timeout=(3.05, 10)). Without one, requests waits forever: when the provider accepts the connection but stops answering, the checkout request hangs indefinitely, holding its worker, and no error or log line ever tells the operator why checkouts stall.
findings.title: Payment call has no timeout

findings.recommendation: Bound the retries (a few attempts with exponential backoff and jitter), retry only transient errors (connection errors, timeouts, 5xx/429) and never 4xx such as a declined card, and send an idempotency key derived from order_id so a retried POST cannot charge twice; raise once retries are exhausted. Today a response lost after the provider charged (read error, 5xx from a proxy) is retried and charges the customer again; a permanent error (400, 401, 402) loops forever at one request per second per order, hammering the provider and never returning to the caller.
findings.title: Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge

findings.recommendation: Log each failed attempt with structured fields (order_id, attempt, HTTP status, provider error code — never the payload's card data or credentials) and raise an actionable error naming the order once retries are exhausted. Today, when the provider is down or rejects the charge, the operator sees no log, no error and no metric: only stuck checkouts.
findings.title: Payment failures are swallowed without a log

findings.recommendation: Read the provider URL from the environment or configuration (e.g. PAYMENT_URL env var). The task was verified against the provider's sandbox, so the URL differs between environments: as written, every environment — dev, staging, tests — sends real charges to the production endpoint, or production must be edited and redeployed to switch provider host.
findings.title: Provider URL hard-coded
